scenes.title: Birds of the Amazon Rainforest
scenes.description: Aves: The Amazon is one of the most biodiverse regions in the world, home to more than 1,300 bird species, representing one-third of all bird species on the planet.

scenes.title: The Amazon River
scenes.description: The Amazon River is the largest river in the world by water discharge, flowing for approximately 6.400 kilometers across South America, It is home to an extraordinary variety of aquatic species and plays a crucial role in the ecosystem.
scenes.imageAlt: The Amazon River seen from the International Space Station

scenes.title: Amazon Storms
scenes.description: Storms and heavy rain are part of the Amazon water cycle. Lightning is most frequent where the atmosphere is unstable, and the forest depends on this water and energy.
scenes.imageAlt: Rain falling over an Amazon river

scenes.title: Deforestation
scenes.description: This point has some of the lowest forest height in the data while tall forest surrounds it: a clearing in the Amazon. Cleared and degraded forest changes the landscape and its ecosystems.
scenes.imageAlt: Cleared forest and fallen trees in the Amazon
